entities.summary: Karl Friedrich von dem Knesebeck was a Prussian field marshal and military adviser in the Napoleonic Wars, best known for designing the campaign plan of the Battle of the Nations and the subsequent invasion of France. As aide-de-camp to the king from 1813, and thereby his closest military advisor, he was a key figure in Prussia's military policy throughout the War of the Sixth Coalition and the subsequent Congress of Vienna. Through his work, von dem Knesebeck contributed significantly to the development of Prussian military strategy and the shaping of European politics in the early 19th century. His influence can be seen in the subsequent reorganization of the German states and the formation of the German Confederation. Von dem Knesebeck's legacy extends beyond his own time, as his tactics and strategies were studied by military leaders for generations to come. The modern-day German military still draws upon the lessons he learned during the Napoleonic Wars, and his name remains synonymous with Prussian military excellence. As a testament to his enduring impact, von dem Knesebeck was posthumously promoted to field marshal and received a state funeral in Berlin. His contributions to Prussian military history were recognized by the German government, and his name remains etched in the annals of military history as one of the most influential field marshals of the Napoleonic era.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Von dem Knesebeck's contributions to Prussian military history were significant, shaping the country's response to the War of the Sixth Coalition and influencing the development of modern Germany. His legacy extends beyond his own time, as his tactics and strategies were studied by military leaders for generations to come.
